justification: LMR attribution flag: expose whether the capacity ceiling was raised by the Housing-SEPP / Low-and-Mid-Rise reforms (vs the base zone tier), and show a one-line note on the card. Conservative by design — the flag is True ONLY when the LMR uplift strictly raises the ceiling above what the base zone+LGA LEP already permits, so we never over-attribute density to LMR.

pre_impl.existing_data: _lmr_uplift_form already runs the live LMR eligibility query and _realistic_forms already takes the denser of base and uplift; both brief paths compute it. The result model had no field recording WHETHER the ceiling came from LMR.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The card could not say why the ceiling was high. Naively flagging 'LMR eligible' would over-claim — many lots reach that density via the base LEP, not LMR.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new query — reuses the uplift already computed. Adds ceiling_from_lmr to the result model, an opt-in return_source kwarg to _realistic_forms (default keeps the 2-tuple so existing callers/tests are unchanged), and a card note.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No new fetching. Fail-safe unchanged: an uplift query failure -> _lmr_uplift_form None -> flag False -> base ceiling -> no note.
pre_impl.frontend_type: TypeScript: ceiling_from_lmr?: boolean|null added; the note renders only when true. tsc --noEmit passes.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: the ceiling gave no reason. After: when LMR genuinely raises the limit, the card adds 'Higher limit available here under the Low & Mid-Rise Housing reforms.' On lots where the base LEP already permits the density (e.g. 14 Stanley, Mascot — verified flag False), no note shows, which is the honest result.

functions.name: _realistic_forms
functions.output: (floor, ceiling) by default; (floor, ceiling, ceiling_from_lmr) when return_source=True
functions.if_none: no uplift / uplift not denser than base -> ceiling_from_lmr False; fail-safe to dwelling_house

values: N/A - no regulatory values; the flag is derived from the already-computed forms.
queries: N/A - no new query; reuses the existing live LMR eligibility result.

break_it.how: fail-safe to the base ceiling with no note; the brief is never blocked
